summary: Checks whether a value is **not** an `Exception`.
description: `nonException(value)` is the same test as `!isException(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
The library's own hierarchy only. A plain `Error` does not qualify, which is exactly what makes the check useful in a `catch` block that has to tell the two apart.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not an `Exception`; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonException(new Error()); // => true
nonException({}); // => true
nonException(null); // => true
nonException(new IllegalArgumentException()); // => false
```
